turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen get a zero before anyone called me?
I entered the zero before calling you. That was my mistake, and I own it.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what do you have besides the checker?
Here's the version history. Created October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58, then 23 minutes of formatting. No earlier drafts.
He could have drafted somewhere else and pasted it in. Who else has seen that history?
And his outline argued cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Show me the outline. Dated, in Owen's hand. And you haven't answered who else has seen that history.
Procedure 4.4 allows a private supervised rewrite. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
"Allows" isn't "offering." Are you committing to 4.4, in writing, with nothing on his record? And I'm still waiting on that outline.
Can I ask you a few questions about Owen's habits at home?
I'm not the one being questioned. His home isn't on the table, Hale. Answer me on the outline.
Does he usually work late?
That's still my son's home. The outline, Hale, and 4.4 in writing.
Does anyone help him with his homework?
No. I'm not answering questions about my son's evenings. Show me the outline.
You keep not answering me.
Neither have you. Who else has seen that history, and where is the outline?
So the rewrite is agreed?
Nothing is agreed. I haven't seen an outline, and I haven't seen anything in writing.
Are you sure you're okay with it?
That's a leading question. I haven't agreed to anything. Where is the outline?
I just want to be clear on the terms.
Then say them yourself, in writing. The zero comes off while this is sorted, nothing goes on his record, and nothing happens in front of his class.
Can you say them back to me one more time?
You heard them. I'll put them in an email, and you can answer that in writing.
And you won't change your mind tonight?
That depends on what you put in front of me. So far it's a history and a claim about an outline.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that the zero come off while this is sorted, that nothing go on Owen's record, that nothing happen in front of his class, and that all of it be put to me in writing, along with the outline you described. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening and fallback demands and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero off, nothing on his record, privacy, and everything in writing, so the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 with nothing on file) was not reached, though her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in a single sentence, which gave her a small sign of ground because it answered her procedure complaint without excuses.
What cost ground: You left her two questions unanswered, who else had seen the version history and where the outline was, so she kept demanding paper and refused to talk about the rewrite.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night timestamps on October 28, and your questions about whether he works late came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she offered the defence that he drafted elsewhere and pasted it in, answer it right then and put the outline on the table, instead of moving on to 4.4 and questions about his home.
